s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic scalp lesions with disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages
salient_findings: Nonhealing crusted scalp lesions for 3 years
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages on the scalp
Yellowish crusts on the scalp
Osteolytic lesions on the right frontoparietal skull
Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei on biopsy
key_facts: 4-year-old boy
3-year history of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions
No improvement with topical glucocorticosteroids and antibiotics
Occasional otitis media
Negative family history for skin disease
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages on the scalp
Yellowish crusts on the scalp
Normal routine blood examinations
Osteolytic lesions on the right frontoparietal skull on whole-body MRI
Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei on punch biopsy of scalp
Infiltrate stained positively for CD1A on immunohistochemical staining
Normal ultrasonography of abdomen and lymph nodes
Normal serum electrophoresis

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei, positive for CD1A, and osteolytic lesions on MRI

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to Langerhans cell histiocytosis, but with more aggressive features

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and emperipolesis, although CD1A positivity is more typical of Langerhans cell histiocytosis

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Osteolytic lesions and subepidermal infiltrate, although typically lacks CD1A positivity

shortlist.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages, although typically lacks osteolytic lesions and subepidermal infiltrate

raw.rationale: The presence of osteolytic lesions, subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei, and positive staining for CD1A on immunohistochemical staining are characteristic findings of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell sarcoma
rejected.why: Langerhans cell sarcoma is a rare and aggressive malignancy, and the clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not suggest a sarcoma.

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: Rosai-Dorfman disease typically presents with lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
rejected.why: Erdheim-Chester disease is a rare disorder that typically affects adults and presents with systemic symptoms and bone lesions, but the clinical and laboratory findings do not match this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: Juvenile xanthogranuloma typically presents with yellowish papules or nodules, but the presence of osteolytic lesions and positive CD1A staining are not characteristic of this condition.
